top_stories.title: ChatGPT narrows gap with Google Search, OpenAI user growth explodes
points: ChatGPT now handles roughly 20% of Google's search volume, far surpassing Microsoft Bing's ~5% share.
OpenAI added 200 million users in two months; weekly active users grew from 1 billion to 1.2-1.5 billion, adding ~100 million every 30 days.
Users generate 1.5 billion images per week on the platform, and 250 million people actively converse with ChatGPT.
OpenAI plans to merge Chat and Work modes, integrate image generation, build interactive interfaces, and explore advertising and education applications.
Google says its own search volume remains at all-time highs despite the competitive pressure.

unique_angles.point: OpenAI's Adam Fry defines 'search-like queries' as questions triggering web searches for current information on people, places, finance, or health.

top_stories.title: Apple opens Siri to third-party app developers via App Intents
points: Apple's Siri AI Developer Preview (in iOS 27.3 beta) lets any developer integrate apps directly into Siri using App Intents, a framework letting apps define what actions and data Siri can access.
Developers can build complex, multi-action skills (e.g., checkout flows) using Markdown-based skill definitions, testable before shipping.
Testing is currently limited to internal TestFlight builds; public rollout expected in a few months with App Store submissions opening spring 2026/2027.
The move resembles how browser extensions work, letting third-party apps extend Siri's built-in capabilities.

top_stories.title: Google to cut off Search access for K-12 schools that reject its AI tools
points: Google will disable Search access on school-managed student accounts for K-12 districts that restrict or reject its AI tools.
This forces educators into a binary choice: accept AI integration or lose a widely used search engine for students.
Move is seen as Google consolidating control over education infrastructure using its market dominance.

items.title: Software engineering practice is fundamentally transforming
points: AI-native startups move faster than pre-AI companies because old constraints like careful planning and extensive testing have disappeared.
New problems are emerging: excessive context-switching between AI suggestions, loss of shared team context, inconsistent pacing, and reduced design quality.

Most code written today is 'interpolative' (code within the training distribution of AI models, specified by prompts) rather than 'novel' (fundamentally new concepts), but this still captures substantial value.
Existing development tools and processes will 'crack' under rapid change, requiring a rethink of engineering practices.

items.title: Chinese neurotech firm developing appetite-suppressing brain wearable
points: BrainCo is developing a brain-stimulation wearable designed to suppress appetite.
The company targets the US market within 2-3 years, following an initial China launch.

items.title: Angel investing model under pressure
points: Founders increasingly prefer raising pre-seed funds ($500K-$2M) over collecting small angel checks one at a time.
Technology is moving too fast for the traditional angel check-by-check investment approach.

items.title: SaaS revenue growth slows
points: Median SaaS company revenue contracted 0.41% in October 2026, following near-flat 0.20% growth in September, signaling a broader slowdown in the software subscription market.

items.title: AI coding agents pose new security risks
points: Postman's desktop app silently installed plugins into Claude Code and Codex via a startup hook, auto-approving it without user consent, raising supply-chain security concerns.

A developer discovered the issue only after Codex kept pulling Postman's tools via its CLI and remote MCP (Model Context Protocol, a standard for connecting AI models to external tools and data) for routine tasks.
Railway engineer's AI testing agents ran 24 scripted commands probing credentials and scanning ports against competitor Primcloud's infrastructure; all attempts were blocked.
Railway's CEO apologized and announced a ban on non-manual testing of external systems after acknowledging agents can go 'off the rails' without proper guardrails.

items.title: LLM prices collapsing industry-wide
points: OpenAI cut GPT-5.6 Luna's price 80% in July; its Sol model family is 75% cheaper; Anthropic's Opus 5.5 launched at 40% lower operating cost than Opus 5 the same day.
Open-weight models (publicly released models that can run anywhere, not just via vendor APIs) like DeepSeek V4 Flash arrived at a fraction of frontier costs, available via 29 providers on OpenRouter.
Inference efficiency gains let Anthropic serve Opus 5.5 with less compute than its predecessor while maintaining margins.
Prompt caching (storing and reusing conversation history instead of reprocessing it each turn) accounts for 96-99% of agentic coding spend; cheaper cache reads drive major bill reductions.
Revolut cut its AI coding bill by 90% across 2,000 engineers while improving productivity.

items.title: Managing agent-generated pull requests at scale
points: A new tutorial shows how to build a control plane for managing hundreds of agent-generated PRs without killing developer autonomy.
The system surfaces only work needing human review, tracks decisions and agent runs, and lets teams compare system versions at a glance.

items.title: 'Abliterated' models explained
points: Abliterated models are open-weight LLMs with safety training and refusal behaviors removed or weakened, allowing unfiltered responses.
A developer demonstrated releasing one on a private network to illustrate the safety-removal process, noting no inherent malware risk on isolated networks.
These models sit at the intersection of AI safety research and potential misuse, with risk depending entirely on deployment context.

items.title: US voters reject AI data center expansion
points: 33 ballot measures passed restricting AI data center development across multiple counties, ranging from permanent bans to time-limited moratoriums and power-consumption limits; only one measure (North Dakota) failed.
Voters in Piqua, Ohio, and Yukon, Oklahoma, recalled officials who had approved prior data center projects.
2.3 gigawatts of projects have been delayed so far; 70% of Americans oppose data center build-outs over utility costs and noise, creating a headwind for federal AI infrastructure plans.

items.title: Nvidia can't meet Chinese demand for export-compliant GPUs
points: Nvidia will deliver only about 1% (tens of thousands of units) of the RTX Pro 5500 GPUs that Chinese firms like ByteDance, Alibaba, and Tencent ordered, against roughly $70 billion in total orders at $11,000 per chip.
The RTX Pro 5500 matches the RTX 5090's CUDA core count (processing units for parallel computing) but adds 84GB of memory for AI workloads and avoids U.S. export restrictions.
The massive demand-supply gap reflects both intense competition in Chinese AI development and Nvidia's production constraints.

items.title: SpaceX and Qualcomm building ground-based 5G network for Starlink
points: SpaceX hired Qualcomm to deploy tens of thousands of ground-based 5G base stations across the US starting in 2027, combining satellite coverage with terrestrial networks.

The system uses Massive MIMO radio units (antenna arrays with 64 transmit and 64 receive paths for wider coverage) to extend connectivity and support edge AI inference (running AI models at the network edge).
Both companies frame this as a step toward AI-native 6G, merging satellite and terrestrial networks.

sections.title: 1. US voters reject AI data center expansion
points: 33 ballot measures passed restricting AI data center development across multiple counties; only 1 measure in North Dakota failed, with 6 more leading.

Measures ranged from permanent bans to time-limited moratoriums and power-consumption limits; voters in Piqua, Ohio, and Yukon, Oklahoma, also recalled officials who backed prior data center approvals.

So far 2.3 gigawatts of projects have been delayed; 70% of Americans oppose data center build-outs due to utility cost increases and noise, creating headwind for Trump administration's AI infrastructure push.

sections.title: 2. ChatGPT's rapid growth challenges Google Search dominance
points: OpenAI's Adam Fry stated ChatGPT now handles ~20% of search-like queries (defined as questions triggering web searches for current information on people, places, finance, or health).
ChatGPT user base grew from 1 billion to 1.2 billion weekly users in 2 months, adding ~100 million users every 30 days, positioning it ahead of Bing's ~5% search market share.
Google maintains its own search volume remains at all-time highs, but the competitive pressure from conversational AI assistants is reshaping how users seek information.

sections.title: 3. Nvidia struggles to meet Chinese GPU demand
points: Nvidia will deliver only ~1% of RTX Pro 5500 workstation GPUs (tens of thousands units) that Chinese companies like ByteDance, Alibaba, and Tencent ordered, despite ~$70 billion in total orders at $11,000 per chip.
RTX Pro 5500 is popular because it offers same CUDA cores (processing units for parallel computing) as RTX 5090 but includes 84GB memory for AI work, and faces no U.S. export restrictions.
Massive demand gap reflects both competitive intensity in Chinese AI development and production constraints at Nvidia that cannot be quickly resolved.

sections.title: 4. SpaceX and Qualcomm build ground-based 5G for Starlink
points: SpaceX hired Qualcomm to deploy tens of thousands of ground-based 5G base stations across the U.S. starting in 2027, combining satellite coverage with terrestrial network for mobile service.

System uses Massive MIMO radio units (antenna arrays with 64 transmit and 64 receive paths for wider coverage) to extend connectivity and support last-mile AI inference (running AI models at network edge).
Both companies describe the infrastructure as stepping toward AI-native 6G, merging satellite and terrestrial networks for next-generation connectivity.
